newsitem.title: FRANCE: HUNGARY INVITED TO JOIN IEA ENERGY WATCHDOG.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY INVITED TO JOIN IEA ENERGY WATCHDOG.

text.p: Hungary is being invited into the International Energy Agency, becoming the first former East Bloc nation to join the club of major world oil consumers, the IEA said on Wednesday.

The multinational agency, part of the Paris-based Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, said its governing board had formally invited Hungary to join at one of its regular sessions on Wednesday.
"The (board) has decided that Hungary is able and willing to meet the requirements of the International Energy Programme," the IEA's founding agreement, a statement said.

The IEA was set up during the world oil crisis in 1974 as a way of sharing emergency oil supplies between Western nations following a boycott by Arab producers and panic buying of oil the year before.
Now, with oil supplies relatively secure, the IEA concentrates mainly on statistical work and promoting free-market ideals for energy among its 23 member nations.
Like many IEA members, Hungary leans on imports for a large share of its energy needs. It imports 55 percent of its annual gas consumption, mostly from Russia.
Hungary cleared the way for IEA membership when it joined the OECD in May this year. OECD membership is a pre-condition.
Diplomats have said Hungary considers membership of the OECD, and to a lesser extent its smaller energy arm, as a stepping stone to membership of the European Union.
Hungarian officials said earlier this year that accession talks with the EU would start after the EU's inter-governmental conference which started in March. 161633 GMT oct 96
